operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2 designated the Chairman or Acting Chairman of the Federal Power Commission to sign permits issued under section 1(a)(3). Executive Order 12038 section 2(a) amended Executive Order 10485 'by deleting Section 2 thereof' (held text, 43 FR 4957); the amendment is effective as of October 1, 1977 under section 6 of Executive Order 12038 (the Department of Energy Organization Act's effective date), not on the signing date, February 3, 1978. The actor is the President by Executive Order 12038 and the mechanism is an amendment that deletes the section, so the clause ended on 1977-10-01. The Code prints Executive Order 10485 as amended without a section 2 (CURRENT:EO:10485#0), which confirms the deletion. The inclusive and exclusive readings of the date coincide because the deletion takes effect on that day.

§  643.914 Purchase of cottonseed  
products by CCC. * *  *
(b) Conditional tenders.  (1) The  
crusher may condition any tender of  
cottonseed products under paragraph
(a)* of this section upon an immediate  
repurchase by the crusher from CCC of  
a specified quantity of cake or meal in­
cluded in such tender, at the current  
market price of cake or meal as deter­
mined by the PMA commodity office.  
CCC reserves the right to reject any or  
all such conditional tenders and any  
acceptance by CCC shall be made with­
in 24 hours after receipt of the tender  
in the PMA commodity office. CCC may  
announce from time to time its policy  
for acceptance or rejection of condi­
tional tenders.
(2) In submitting any tender the  
crusher may incorporate in the tender  
an offer to repurchase a specified quan­
tity and quality of linters included in  
such tender at the applicable price for  
linters listed in §  643.915 and CCC shall  
accept such offer to purchase upon its  
determination that the price contained  
in the offer to purchase is the applicable  
price.

The permits issued under Executive Order 8202 were preserved by section 4, which is a separate clause that continues.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10485 of September 3, 1953 (18 FR 5397; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10485.txt, read in full) designates the Federal Power Commission to receive applications for, and issue, Presidential permits for border facilities for electric energy and natural gas (section 1), lets the Chairman sign them (section 2), authorizes rules (section 3), preserves existing permits (section 4) and revokes Executive Order 8202 (section 5). The held page text of section 1(a)(3) is interrupted by the issue's contents and masthead pages; the packet's 10,449-character machine clause across them is replaced by two clauses and the other machine clauses are kept (inventory override of ten clauses). Own terms: no section has an end date. Later instruments: Executive Order 12038 section 2(a) (43 FR 4957, effective October 1, 1977 under its section 6) deleted section 2 and substituted the Secretary of Energy for the Federal Power Commission in sections 1, 3 and 4; it is recorded as a later event on sections 1, 1(b), 3 and 4 and as the end of section 2. The Office of the Federal Register note 'Revokes: EO 8202, July 13, 1939 | Amended by: EO 12038, February 3, 1978 | See: EO 11423, August 16, 1968; EO 12847, May 17, 1993; EO 13337, April 30, 2004' was reconciled: Executive Order 11423 (as amended by 12847), Executive Order 13337 and Executive Order 13867 (2019) each except facilities covered by Executive Order 10485 from the Secretary of State's permit designation, so they recite this order and neither amend, revoke nor supersede it (Executive Order 13867 revokes Executive Orders 13337 and 11423, not this order). The packet's lead 'cited by number, no change provision located: EO:11062' was not confirmed by a search of the held text of Executive Order 11062 for this order's number. Current law: current-law:usc has 6 hits (15 U.S.C. 717b note printing the order as amended by Executive Order 12038, and other Code references), current-law:ecfr has 10 hits (including 18 CFR 153.1 and 153.15), later-events:ofr_catalog 4 hits; no search shows an ending. The U.S. Code edition searched is release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Section 2 ended earlier than the rest: it was deleted by Executive Order 12038, effective 1977-10-01. Section 5 was performed on issuance, 1953-09-03. Sections 1, 3 and 4 have no end; the Code prints them as amended.","independent_command_check":"Section 1 (designation), section 2 (signing), section 3 (rules), section 4 (permit savings) and section 5 (revocation of Executive Order 8202) are independent; section 2's deletion and section 5's performance do not end the others.","savings_check":"Section 4 is the savings clause and continues; section 5's revocation does not affect permits saved by section 4.","scope_check":"The ten clauses cover every operative sentence from section 1 through section 5 (the recitals before 'NOW, THEREFORE', the signature and the issue pages between the two halves of section 1(a)(3) are outside them)."}

savings_residuals.reason: Section 4 preserves permits issued under Executive Order 8202 and under this order until modified or revoked; those permits continue and are administered under 18 CFR part 153. The revocation of Executive Order 8202 in section 5 was performed in 1953 and leaves no further duty.

M ISCELLANEO US A M E N D M EN T S
The regulations of Commodity Credit  
Corporation with respect to the pur­
chase of cottonseed products as a means  
of supporting the price of 1953-crop cot­
tonseed (1953 CCC Cottonseed Bulletin 3, 
(18 F. R. 3988,4875) ), are hereby amend­
ed by additions to §  643.912 (b), §  643.913
(a) and (d) and by changing paragraph
(b) of §  643.914 thereof as follows:
1. Section 643.912 (b) Source  is
amended by adding the words “Revision  
1  as amended” to “1953 Cottonseed Bul­
letin V’  wherever it appears in that  
Paragraph.
2. Section 643.913 (a) Price and (d)  
Receipts from gins owned by or under  
same legal entity as the crusher  are  
amended by adding the words “as
amended” to “1953 Cottonseed Bulletin  
2” where it appears in paragraphs (a)  
and (d) of this section.
3. Section 643.914 (b) is amended to  
read as follows:
§  643.914 Purchase of cottonseed  
products by CCC. * *  *
(b) Conditional tenders.  (1) The  
crusher may condition any tender of  
cottonseed products under paragraph
(a)* of this section upon an immediate  
repurchase by the crusher from CCC of  
a specified quantity of cake or meal in­
cluded in such tender, at the current  
market price of cake or meal as deter­
mined by the PMA commodity office.  
CCC reserves the right to reject any or  
all such conditional tenders and any  
acceptance by CCC shall be made with­
in 24 hours after receipt of the tender  
in the PMA commodity office. CCC may  
announce from time to time its policy  
for acceptance or rejection of condi­
tional tenders.
(2) In submitting any tender the  
crusher may incorporate in the tender  
an offer to repurchase a specified quan­
tity and quality of linters included in  
such tender at the applicable price for  
linters listed in §  643.915 and CCC shall  
accept such offer to purchase upon its  
determination that the price contained  
in the offer to purchase is the applicable  
price.

“ Sec. 5.1. C iv il S ervice R e g u la tio n s . The Director, Office o f Personnel Man­
agement, shall promulgate and enforce regulations necessary to carry out the

continuation o f the conditions which gave rise to it. Like variations shall be

tive orders imposing responsibilities on the Office by:
(a) Investigating the qualifications and suitability o f applicants for posi­
tions in the competitive service. The Director may require appointments to be

(b) Evaluating the effectiveness of: (1) personnel policies, programs, and 
operations o f Executive and other Federal agencies subject to the jurisdiction 
o f the Office, including their effectiveness with regard to merit selection and 
employee development; (2) agency compliance with and enforcement o f appli­
cable laws, rules, regulations and office directives; and (3) agency personnel 
management evaluation systems.
(c) Investigating, or directing an agency to investigate and report on, 
apparent violations o f applicable laws, rules, regulations, or directives requir­
ing corrective action, found in the course o f an evaluation.
(d) Requiring agencies to report, in a manner and at times as the Director 
may prescribe, personnel information the Director requests relating to civilian 
employees in the Executive branch o f the Government, as defined by Section 
311 o f the Civil Service Reform Act o f 1978, including positions and officers 
and employees in the competitive, excepted and Senior Executive services, 
whether permanent, career-conditional, temporary or emergency.
“ Sec. 5.3. E n forcem en t.
(a) The Director is authorized to ensure enforcement o f the civil service 
laws, rules, and regulations, and all applicable Executive orders, by:
( 1  ) Instructing an agency to separate or take other action against an 
employee serving an appointment subject to investigation when the Director 
finds that the employee is disqualified for Federal employment. Where the 
employee or the agency appeals the Director’s finding that a separation or 
other action is necessary, the Director may instruct the agency as to whether 
or not the employee should remain on duty and continue to receive pay 
pending adjudication o f the appeal: P ro v id e d , That when an agency separates 
or takes other action against an employee pursuant to thé Director’s instruc­
tions, and the Director, on the basis o f new evidence, subsequently reverses

agency shall, upon request o f the Director, restore the employee to duty or 
otherwise reverse any action taken.
(2) Reporting the results o f evaluation or investigations to the head o f the 
agency concerned with instructions for any corrective action necessary, includ­
ing cancellation o f personnel actions where appropriate. The Director’s find­

(b) Whenever the Director issues specific instructions as to separation or 
other corrective action with regard to an employee, including cancellation o f a 
personnel action, the head o f the agency concerned shall comply with the 
Director’s instructions.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2(b) designates the Civil Service Commission to perform the functions conferred on the President by section 6 of the act for allotments and assignments under section 5 of the act. Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404) substituted 'Office of Personnel Management' for 'Civil Service Commission' in the orders listed in its section 2-101, which includes this order (the list prints the number as '19982' in the scan, which is an OCR error for 10982 between 10973 and 11103) (before: Civil Service Commission; after: Office of Personnel Management). Executive Order 12748 section 5 (56 FR 4521; signed February 1, 1991) then amended section 2(b) 'to read as follows': the Office of Personnel Management performs the functions under 5 U.S.C. 5527 for allotments and assignments under 5 U.S.C. 5525 and advance payments to new appointees under 5 U.S.C. 5524a as added by section 107(a) of the Federal Employees Pay Comparability Act of 1990 (before: allotments and assignments only, under the act's section 5; after: those plus advance payments to new appointees). Under its section 9(b) the order takes effect May 4, 1991 (the Office of Personnel Management may set an earlier date not before February 3, 1991; I found no such determination in the held texts, so the default date is used). The clause is amended, not ended, and the Code prints the amended text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10982 of December 25, 1961 (27 FR 3; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10982.txt, read in full, characters 540-5550) administers the Act of September 26, 1961 on evacuation payments. The packet's ten machine clauses did not follow the sections; I read the whole order and replaced them by twelve clauses: the recital, 1(a), 1(b), 1(c), 2(a), 2(b), the section 3 lead, 3(a), 3(b), 3(c), 4(a) and 4(b). Later instruments, both official texts held in the packet: Executive Order 12107 (December 28, 1978, effective January 1, 1979), which substitutes the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission in the listed orders, including this one (listed as '19982' in the scan, an OCR error), recorded on each clause that names the Commission; and Executive Order 12748 section 5 (signed February 1, 1991, effective May 4, 1991 by default under its section 9(b)), which restates section 2(b). The Code note at 5 U.S.C. 5527 prints the order as amended by both, and 28 CFR 0.154 and 5 CFR part 550 cite it. None of these ends any clause. Not held in the packet: the text of 5 U.S.C. 5522-5527 beyond the note and the later OPM regulations (5 CFR part 550 subpart D is held in the repo but not in the packet); the claim rests on the Code's printing of the order and the eCFR citations. research_rationale:
Executive Order 12318 of August 21, 1981 (46 FR 42833-42834; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12318.txt, read in full, location confidence high) transfers statistical policy functions from the Secretary of Commerce to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. The packet marked the own-text boundary unresolved and cut the order into 14 fragments; I read the whole order (heading, eight sections, signature and the effective date of August 23, 1981 in section 8) and replaced the inventory by nine clauses: the recital, sections 1, 2, 3, 4(a), 4(b), 5, 6 and sections 7 and 8 together. Section 4(a) (revocation of Executive Order 12013) and section 5 (transfer of records and funds) are one-time commands exhausted when the order took effect on 1981-08-23; the amendments in sections 1, 2, 3 and 4(b) are embodied in the Code's printing of Executive Orders 11541, 10253, 10033 and 11961 as amended by Executive Order 12318 (CURRENT:EO:12318#4, #3, #1, #2); sections 6 and 7 are open-ended and no held source ends them. Later instruments: Executive Order 12518 (June 3, 1985; official text in the packet) amended Executive Order 11961 outside section 4, and is recorded as a later event on section 4(b); the other orders amended (11541, 10253, 10033) show no later amendment in the Code notes beyond those predating 1981 and this order. A search of the held texts for the number 12318 finds the order's copies, the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification, and Federal Register or CFR authority lines (15 CFR part 801; 15 CFR parts cite E.O. 11961 as amended by E.O. 12318) that treat the order as in force; none amends, revokes or supersedes it. Current law: current-law:usc 8 hits (the Code notes above), current-law:ecfr 1 hit (15 CFR part 801 authority line), later-events:ofr_catalog 0 hits.

Section 1. Amendments to Executive Order 9158. Executive Order 9158 
of May 11, 1942 (Air Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9242–A 
of September 11, 1942 (Amending Executive Order No. 9158 of May 11, 
1942, to Provide that the Air Medal May Be Awarded to Persons Serving 
with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard of the United States), 
is further amended as follows: 
(a) The first paragraph is amended— 
(i) by striking ‘‘Army and Navy’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘Armed 
Forces’’; 
(ii) by striking ‘‘any person’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘those individ-
uals’’; 
(iii) by inserting ‘‘Air Force, Space Force,’’ after ‘‘Marine Corps,’’; and 
(iv) by striking ‘‘distinguishes, or has distinguished, himself’’ and inserting 
in lieu thereof ‘‘distinguish, or have distinguished, themselves’’. 
(b) The second paragraph is amended— 
(i) by amending the first sentence to read as follows: ‘‘The Air Medal 
and appurtenances thereto shall be of appropriate design approved by 
the Secretary of Defense and, under such regulations as the Secretaries 
of the military departments may prescribe, may be awarded by the Secretary 
of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force, 
or the Secretary of Homeland Security with respect to the Coast Guard 
when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, or by such commanding 
officers of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, or 
Coast Guard as the said Secretaries may respectively designate.’’; and 
(ii) in the second sentence, by striking ‘‘his jurisdiction’’ and inserting 
in lieu thereof ‘‘the jurisdiction of the Navy’’. 
(c) The following new paragraph is added at the end of the Executive 
Order: ‘‘The regulations of the Secretaries of the military departments con-
cerned with respect to the award of the Air Medal shall, so far as practicable, 
be uniform and shall be subject to the approval of the Secretary of Defense.’’.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 amends EO 9158 (Air Medal), as amended by EO 9242-A, extending the Air Medal to the Armed Forces including the Air Force and the Space Force, with gender-neutral wording, new award authorities and a paragraph on uniform regulations. It was effective on signing, 2022-10-03, and has no end date or ending condition; the amended order is printed in the U.S. Code with the amendment embodied, and nothing held ends it, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14.

EO 14085 (signed 2022-10-03; 87 FR 60541; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14085.txt, read in full) amends six earlier orders on military decorations and awards (EO 9158 Air Medal, EO 8809 Good Conduct Medal, EO 10694 unit citations, EO 11046 Bronze Star Medal, EO 13830 delegation of authority to approve decorations, EO 11545 Defense Distinguished Service Medal) to cover the Space Force and to use gender-neutral and updated wording, and adds general provisions. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The packet inventory fragmented the sections, so it is replaced by eight clauses (inventory override). Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition, and the order has no effective-date section, so each amendment took effect on signing. Later instruments: the held-text number search finds only the order's own Federal Register copies, the dossier chain lists no event, and the ofr_catalog search records no disposition note naming it. Current law: the U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected) prints each amended order with a status line naming EO 14085: EO 9158 as amended by section 1, EO 8809 by section 2, EO 10694 by section 3 and EO 13830 by section 5 in notes under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57; EO 11046 as amended by section 4 in a note under 10 U.S.C. 7276; and EO 11545 as amended by section 6 in a note under 10 U.S.C. 1125. The 7276 note also records that paragraph (a) of section 4 could not be executed because EO 13286 had already made that identical amendment. The eCFR search has 0 hits. No section is found ended.

THE PRESIDENT 915
Executive Order 11448  
ESTABLISHING THE MERITORIOUS SERVICE MEDAL
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United 
States and as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces of the United 
States, it is ordered as follows:
S ection  1. There is hereby established a Meritorious Service Medal, 
with acompanying ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secre­
tary of a military department or the Secretary of Transportation with 
regard to the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, 
or by such military commanders, or other appropriate officers as the 
Secretary concerned may designate, to any member of the armed forces 
of the United States, who has distinguished himself by outstanding 
meritorious achievement or service to the United States.
S ec. 2. The Meritorious Service Medal and appurtenances thereto 
shall be of appropriate design approved by the Secretary of Defense, 
and shall be awarded under such regulations as the Secretary con­
cerned may prescribe. Such regulations shall, so far as practicable, be 
uniform, and those of the military departments shall be subject to the 
approval of the Secretary of Defense.
S ec. 3. No more than one Meritorious Service Medal shall be awarded 
to any one person, but for each succeeding outstanding meritorious 
achievement or service justifying such an award a suitable device may 
be awarded to be worn with the medal as prescribed by appropriate 
regulations.
S ec. 4. The Meritorious Service Medal or device may be awarded 
posthumously and, when so awarded, may be presented to such repre­
sentative of the deceased as may be deemed appropriate by the Secre­
tary of the department concerned.

or by such military commanders, or other appropriate officers as the 
Secretary concerned may designate, to any member of the armed forces 
of the United States, who has distinguished himself by outstanding 
meritorious achievement or service to the United States.
S ec. 2. The Meritorious Service Medal and appurtenances thereto 
shall be of appropriate design approved by the Secretary of Defense, 
and shall be awarded under such regulations as the Secretary con­
cerned may prescribe. Such regulations shall, so far as practicable, be 
uniform, and those of the military departments shall be subject to the 
approval of the Secretary of Defense.
S ec. 3. No more than one Meritorious Service Medal shall be awarded 
to any one person, but for each succeeding outstanding meritorious 
achievement or service justifying such an award a suitable device may 
be awarded to be worn with the medal as prescribed by appropriate 
regulations.
S ec. 4. The Meritorious Service Medal or device may be awarded 
posthumously and, when so awarded, may be presented to such repre­
sentative of the deceased as may be deemed appropriate by the Secre­
tary of the department concerned.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1-102 says that until the Office of Personnel Management is established (on or before January 1, 1979), pursuant to Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, the Civil Service Commission shall exercise the authority delegated under the order. The condition occurred on January 1, 1979: the held text of Executive Order 12107, section 1-101, makes the establishment of the Office of Personnel Management under the Reorganization Plan effective on that date, and section 1-102's own wording sets that date as the latest. The actor is the order itself (own terms); the first end is the date the Office of Personnel Management was established, January 1, 1979, so the Civil Service Commission's exercise ended then. The inclusive reading (the clause runs through the end of December 31, 1978) and the alternative reading (the clause ends when January 1, 1979 begins) coincide in practice because the condition is the establishment of a body on that day.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12109 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1067; held official text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12109.txt, read in full) has two numbered sections. Section 1-101 designates the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to exercise the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5948 to prescribe regulations, criteria and conditions for payment of comparability allowances to recruit and retain certain Federal physicians. Section 1-102 provides that, until the Office of Personnel Management is established (on or before January 1, 1979) under Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, the Civil Service Commission exercises that authority. The packet inventory already separates the two sections, so no inventory correction was needed. Section 1-102 ended by its own terms when the Office of Personnel Management was established: the held text of Executive Order 12107 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12107.txt), section 1-101, provides that the establishment of the Office of Personnel Management under sections 101 and 103 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 is effective on January 1, 1979. Executive Order 12107 does not amend Executive Order 12109 and is cited only for that date. Section 1-101 has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. current-law:usc has 1 hit, the U.S. Code note that prints this order under 5 U.S.C. 5948, with no ending statement. current-law:ecfr has 1 hit, 5 CFR part 595 (Physicians' Comparability Allowances), whose authority line cites E.O. 12109, 44 FR 1067, Jan. 3, 1979 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t5-part595.txt). later-events:ofr_catalog has 0 hits and the Office of the Federal Register catalog record carries no disposition note. A search of the held texts for the number 12109 finds only the order's own copies, the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_12109.txt, which records no later instrument) and 5 CFR part 595; none amends, revokes or supersedes the order. The authority statute 5 U.S.C. 5948 (held text jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s5948.txt) is in force: its 2000 amendments (Pub. L. 106-571, section 2(a)(1)) struck the earlier sentence that barred agreements after a fixed date, and subsection (a) still refers to regulations that the President or his designee may prescribe. The U.S. Code edition searched is release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in it.
